content_blocks.title: Why this matters
content_blocks.text: A regular expression describes a pattern; literal characters often need escaping. The example is intentionally small so you can predict its result before checking it in a local R session.

content_blocks.title: Work through it
content_blocks.text: Test a pattern against matching and non-matching strings before using it on a full dataset. Change one input or condition at a time, compare the observed result with your prediction, and write down one limitation.

content_blocks.title: Common pitfall
content_blocks.text: Do not treat a syntactically plausible example as proof of correctness. For regular expressions, check the input type, missing/empty cases, output shape, and domain assumptions.

common_mistakes.problem: Using an example without checking its inputs or output shape.
common_mistakes.why: R can coerce types, propagate missing values or simplify results unexpectedly.
common_mistakes.fix: Inspect with str(), class(), typeof(), length() or dim() and add a direct check.
